projects.title: DICEON — Play & Win
projects.summary: A bold mobile interface for games, rewards and everyday discovery.
projects.body:
DICEON — Play & Win is a mobile gaming interface built around game discovery and rewards. The project combines a distinctive emerald identity with dark surfaces, rounded cards and a compact navigation system.
This case study pairs the archived interface with new presentation studies to explain its visual structure.

sections.title: The interface, at a glance.
sections.body: An emerald identity anchors a dark gaming interface. The archive brings together welcome and registration screens, game selection, balances and rewards destinations.

sections.title: Three decisions that shape the experience.
sections.body: A focused entry screen keeps account actions separate from game browsing. Game rows place player counts and coin entry values beside the Play action. The rewards hub groups balances and activities into a repeated card structure.

process.title: From structure to screen.
process.body: A reconstructed exploration of the archived interface: the entry point, the game library and the rewards hub. These studies make the layout decisions visible.

projects.title: YaLLa Compass · Qatar Finals 2025
projects.summary: Designing the space around the competition.
projects.body:
A Qatar event design project spanning on-site venue study, spectator experience planning, stage design and 3D visualisation.
I worked from the venue and its constraints toward a connected event environment: audience seating, team booths, broadcast positions, sponsor spaces and the stage itself.

eventStudy.context: The challenge was to connect the spectacle on stage with the experience around it: where visitors spend time, what they can see, and how competition, sponsors and production share the venue.

eventContext.title: Designed for a live event. The competition moved online.
paragraphs: YaLLa Compass is a Counter-Strike 2 circuit organised by YaLLa Esports. Qatar was announced as one of its two flagship 2025 destinations, combining elite competition with a live venue experience.

The initial Qatar event window was 15–20 April 2025. In an update dated 14 March 2025, the organiser moved the planned LAN grand final to 19 April and described the finals as a private VIP event. These dates reflect successive announcements, rather than one unchanged schedule.

The planned in-person Qatar finals were subsequently moved online. The organiser cited unexpected scheduling constraints in the global Counter-Strike calendar and a need to protect competitive integrity and long-term stability. It confirmed a ranked online tournament on European servers with a $300,000 prize pool.

The competition continued: the organiser’s later schedule placed the group stage on 17 April and playoffs on 19–20 April 2025, and its recap named NAVI Junior as champion. The physical event concept shown here should therefore be read as design development for the planned LAN, rather than documentation of a completed venue build.

home.introHeading: {{yearsWord}} years designing how Pakistani esports looks.
introParas: I am Rabees Sheikh, an art director and creative designer with extensive experience in the esports industry in Pakistan. I design 2D and 3D graphics and UI/UX, most recently as Senior Creative Manager at Next Generation Esports, directing branding, social campaigns and event graphics for Free Fire Esports Pakistan.

The work runs from tournament identity to LAN stage visualisation to the graphics that go out the same night. Generative video and 3D sit inside that process rather than beside it. Both are used for look development and content, art-directed to the same standard as everything else.

about.heading: Rabees Sheikh, art director and creative designer, Karachi.
intro: Art Director and Creative Designer with extensive experience in the esports industry in Pakistan. Skilled in designing 2D and 3D graphics, as well as UI/UX designing.

Most recently Senior Creative Manager at Next Generation Esports, directing branding, social media campaigns and event graphics for Free Fire Esports Pakistan, and leading a team of designers across the season.
Passionate about creating visually appealing and engaging designs that capture the essence of esports in Pakistan, now extending that practice into 3D visualisation and generative video.

experience.body: Directed a team of ten designers across branding, social media campaigns and event graphics for Free Fire Esports Pakistan, with campaign engagement up 30 per cent. Led the 3D graphics for tournaments that drew over a million views across streaming platforms, designed UI and UX assets that lifted interactions on promotional platforms by 25 per cent, and cut project turnaround by 20 per cent. Trained and mentored five junior designers.
Ran an editorial team of eight writers and designers producing more than twenty exclusive articles a month, and set the content strategy that raised reader retention by 25 per cent.
Designed graphics for esports events including social content, banners, logos and merchandise. Over a hundred pieces across campaigns, with fan engagement up 15 per cent on social platforms.
Studied advertising alongside full-time design work in esports.

recognition.body: Recognised by Next Generation Esports for leadership in directing design teams and delivering branding solutions.
Awarded at Next Generation Esports for results in campaign engagement and visual content creation.
